full_text:
Medi-Court Lawsuit Process
5 Steps to Sue a California Health Plan ($12,500 Max)

1) Exhaust Administrative Remedies
*   Submit a 30-day formal grievance to the health plan
*   File an Independent Medical Review (IMR) with the DMHC

2) Calculate Total Damages
*   Include unpaid Conlan claims and out-of-pocket medical visits
*   Calculate transportation expenses up to the $12,500 individual limit

3) Draft Form SC-100 (Plaintiff's Claim)
*   Cite breach of contract and statutory defaults
*   Reference Health & Safety Code § 1367 and AB 3275

4) File Fee Waiver (Form FW-001)
*   Request 100% waiver of court filing fees ($30-$75)
*   Applies to plaintiffs receiving Medi-Cal or low-income assistance

5) Serve the Registered Agent
*   Locate the official Agent for Service of Process via Secretary of State
*   Formally serve the corporate entity via certified process server or Sheriff

Administrative Default & Action
Public Entity Trap: If suing a public plan like L.A. Care, you MUST file a Government Claim first and receive a formal Notice of Rejection before filing Form SC-100.
